Per line: N = normalized Akkadian reconstruction (| metrical foot, || caesura); T = eBL English translation; L = lemmas with eBL dictionary glosses; then notes, parallel lines, and the manuscripts' transliterations (ATF). Bibliography keys like [RN117: 889] are resolved in bibliography.md (RN117 = George 2003).

1

  • N: itbē-ma | gilgāmeš || šunatam | ipaššar
  • T: Gilgameš arose to reveal a dream,
  • L: itbē-ma ← tebû I “OAkk, Ass. tabā'u(m), NB tabû to get up, arise, set out”; gilgāmeš ← Gilgameš I; šunatam ← šuttu I “pl. šunātu(m) dream š. naṭālu, amāru etc. to have a dream, to…”; ipaššar ← pašāru I “to release, free”
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "SM" a+4'; cf. L I.4 MB "Priv₁" 7; L II.2 SB "I" 243
BabaOB1 i 1. it-be₂-e-ma {d}GIŠ šu-na-tam i-pa-aš-šar

2

  • N: issaqqaram | ana ummīšu
  • T: saying to his mother:
  • L: issaqqaram ← zakāru I “to speak, say”; ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; ummīšu ← ummu I “f. mother”
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "SM" a+4'; cf. L I.4 MB "Priv₁" 7; L I.4 SB "I" 243
BabaOB1 i 2. is-sa₃-qar-am a-na um-mi-šu

3

  • N: ummī | ina šāt (|) mušītīya
  • T: ‘O mother, during the course of this night
  • L: ummī ← ummu I “f. mother”; ina ← ina I “(im-m..., ip-p... etc.) in, on”; šāt ← šāt I “f. sg. who(m), which”; mušītīya ← mušītu I, -ya I, mūšu I “pl. mušiātu, mušâtu night(-time)”
  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 MB "Ur" 62; cf. L I.4 SB "VII" 165; cf. L I.4 SB "I" 244; cf. L II.2 SB "III" 22; cf. L II.2 SB "III" 30
BabaOB1 i 3. um-mi i-na ša-a-at mu-ši-ti-ia

4-5

  • N: šamhākū-ma | attanallak || ina birīt (|) eṭlūtim
  • T: I was walking about lustily in the company of young men.
  • L: šamhākū-ma ← šamāhu I “to grow, flourish”; attanallak ← alāku I “to go”; ina ← ina I “(im-m..., ip-p... etc.) in, on”; birīt ← birītu I “space between, distance partition, dividing baulk (between fields)”; eṭlūtim ← eṭlu I “manly”
BabaOB1 i 4-5. ša-am-ha-ku-ma at-ta-na-al-la-ak | i#-na# bi-ri-it eṭ-lu-tim

6

  • N: ibbīšūnim-ma | kakkabū (|) šamāʾī
  • T: The stars of the sky parted company,
  • L: ibbīšūnim-ma ← bašû I “to be (at hand, available)”; kakkabū ← kakkabu I “star also ref. to planets”; šamāʾī ← šamû I “mostly pl. tant. sky, heaven”
  • Note: The reading of the first word follows [RN116: 72–73].
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "SM" a+5'; L I.4 MB "Priv₁" 8; L I.4 SB "I" 245
BabaOB1 i 6. ib-bi*#-šu*#-nim#-ma ka-ka-bu ša-ma-i

7

  • N: k[i]ṣrum! | ša ānim || imqutam | ana ṣērīya
  • T: a lump of sky-rock fell down before me.
  • L: k[i]ṣrum! ← kiṣru I “pl. usu. m. knot”; ša ← ša I “who(m), which”; ānim ← Anu I “An(um) (the god of heaven) OAkk, Bab.”; imqutam ← maqātu I “to fall”; ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; ṣērīya ← ṣēru I “back, upperside”
  • Note: The reading of the first word follows [RN116: 73].
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "SM" a+6'; L I.4 MB "Priv₁" 9; L I.4 SB "I" 246
BabaOB1 i 7. k[i-i]ṣ!-rum ša a-nim# im-qu₂-tam a-na ṣe-ri-ia

8

  • N: aššīšū-ma | iktabit | elīya
  • T: I picked it up but it grew too heavy for me,
  • L: aššīšū-ma ← našû II “to lift, carry”; iktabit ← kabātu I “to be(come) heavy”; elīya ← eli I “on, over, above”
  • Note: The translation of iktabit follows [NABU2004-49: 51].
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "SM" a+7'; L I.4 MB "Priv₁" 10; L I.4 SB "I" 247
BabaOB1 i 8. aš-ši-šu-ma ik-ta-bi-it e-li-ia

9

  • N: unīssū-ma | nuššašu | ul eltēʾi
  • T: I pushed at it but I could not move it.
  • L: unīssū-ma ← nâšu I “to rock, shift Bab., NA”; nuššašu ← nâšu I “to rock, shift Bab., NA”; ul ← ul I “not Bab., to negate main clause”; eltēʾi ← le'û I “to be able, powerful”
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "SM" a+8'; L I.4 MB "Priv₁" 11; L I.4 SB "I" 248
BabaOB1 i 9. u₂-ni-is₂-su-ma nu-uš-ša-šu u₂-ul el-ti-ʾi

10

  • N: uruk | mātum || pahir | elīšu
  • T: The land of Uruk was gathered about it,
  • L: uruk ← Uruk I; mātum ← mātu I “f. land, country”; pahir ← pahāru II “to gather”; elīšu ← eli I “on, over, above”
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "SM" a+9'; L I.4 MB "Priv₁" 12; L I.4 SB "I" 249; L I.4 SB "I" 277
BabaOB1 i 10. UNUG{ki} ma-tum pa-hi-ir e-li-šu

11

  • N: eṭlūtum | unaššaqū | šēpīšu
  • T: the young men kissing its feet.
  • L: eṭlūtum ← eṭlu I “manly”; unaššaqū ← našāqu I “to kiss”; šēpīšu ← šēpu I “f., often du.”
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "II" 21; cf. L I.4 SB "I" 253
BabaOB1 i 11. eṭ-lu-tum u₂-na-ša-qu₂ ši-pi-šu

12-13

  • N: ummid-ma | pūtī || īmidū | yâti
  • T: I braced my forehead and they supported me,
  • L: ummid-ma ← emēdu I “to lean on”; pūtī ← pūtu I “f.”; īmidū ← emēdu I “to lean on”; yâti ← yâti I “me (1 sg. acc. pron.)”
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "SM" a+11'; L I.4 MB "Priv₁" 14
BabaOB1 i 12-13. u₂-um-mi-id-ma pu-ti | i-mi-du ia-ti

14

  • N: aššiaššū-ma | atbalaššu | ana ṣērīki
  • T: I picked it up and carried it off to you.’
  • L: aššiaššū-ma ← našû II “to lift, carry”; atbalaššu ← wabālu I “(cf. also babālu) to carry, bring”; ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; ṣērīki ← ṣēru I “back, upperside”
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "SM" a+12'; L I.4 MB "Priv₁" 15; L I.4 SB "I" 255; cf. L I.4 SB "I" 263; L I.4 SB "I" 281
BabaOB1 i 14. aš-ši-a-šu-ma at-ba-la-aš-šu a-na ṣe-ri-ki

15

  • N: ummi (|) gilgāmeš || mūdeat (|) kalāma
  • T: The mother of Gilgameš, well versed in everything,
  • L: ummi ← ummu I “f. mother”; gilgāmeš ← Gilgameš I; mūdeat ← mūdû I “pl. mūdû, NB mūdānê”; kalāma ← kalāma I “all (of it) Bab. indeclinable as obj. of vb. or gen. after st. constr.”
  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 OB "SM" a+13'; cf. L I.4 MB "Priv₁" 16-17; cf. L I.4 MB "Priv₁" 38; cf. L I.4 SB "I" 257-258
BabaOB1 i 15. um-mi {d}GIŠ mu-de-a-at ka-la-ma

16

  • N: issaqqaram | ana gilgāmeš
  • T: said to Gilgameš:
  • L: issaqqaram ← zakāru I “to speak, say”; ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; gilgāmeš ← Gilgameš I
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "SM" a+14'; L I.4 MB "Priv₁" 17; cf. L I.4 SB "I" 258
BabaOB1 i 16. is-sa₃-qar-am a-na {d}GIŠ

17

  • N: minde | gilgāmeš | ša kīma kâti
  • T: ‘For sure, Gilgameš, one like yourself
  • L: minde ← minde I “perhaps Bab., Am., Bogh.”; gilgāmeš ← Gilgameš I; ša ← ša I “who(m), which”; kīma ← kīma I “like”; kâti ← kâti I “you (2 sg. pron.) Bab.”
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "SM" a+15'; L I.4 MB "Priv₁" 18
BabaOB1 i 17. mi-in-de {d}GIŠ ša ki-ma ka-ti

18-19

  • N: ina ṣēri(m) | iwwalid-ma || urabbīšu | šadû
  • T: was born in the wild and the upland reared him.
  • L: ina ← ina I “(im-m..., ip-p... etc.) in, on”; ṣēri(m) ← ṣēru I “back, upperside”; iwwalid-ma ← alādu I “to give birth (to)”; urabbīšu ← rabû II “to be big, to grow”; šadû ← šadû I “st. constr. šad(i)”
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "SM" a+16'; L I.4 MB "Priv₁" 19
BabaOB1 i 18-19. i-na ṣe-ri i-wa-li-id-ma | u₂-ra-ab-bi-šu ša-du-u₂

20

  • N: tammaršū-ma | tahaddu | attā
  • T: You will see him and you will rejoice,
  • L: tammaršū-ma ← amāru I “to see”; tahaddu ← hadû III “to be joyful, rejoice”; attā ← attā I “you (2 m. sg. pron.)”
  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 OB "SM" a+21'; cf. L I.4 MB "Priv₁" 24
BabaOB1 i 20. ta-mar-šu-ma ta-ha-du at-ta

21

  • N: eṭlūtum | unaššaqū | šēpīšu
  • T: the young men will kiss his feet.
  • L: eṭlūtum ← eṭlu I “manly”; unaššaqū ← našāqu I “to kiss”; šēpīšu ← šēpu I “f., often du.”
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "II" 11; cf. L I.4 SB "I" 253; L I.4 SB "II" 107
BabaOB1 i 21. eṭ-lu-tum u₂-na-ša-qu₂ ši-pi-šu!

22-23

  • N: teddiraššū-ma | tatarrâššu | ana ṣērīya
  • T: You will hug him and bring him to me.’
  • L: teddiraššū-ma ← edēru I “to embrace, wrap o.s. round O/jB”; tatarrâššu ← warû II “to lead”; ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; ṣērīya ← ṣēru I “back, upperside”
  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 OB "SM" a+22'; L I.4 MB "Priv₁" 25
BabaOB1 i 22-23. te-ed-di-ra-aš!?#-<<x#>>-šu#-u₂-ma | ta#-tar-ra-aš-šu# a#-na# ṣe-ri#-ia#

24

  • N: [i]ttīlam-ma | ītamar | šanītam
  • T: He lay down and saw another dream.
  • L: [i]ttīlam-ma ← nâlu I “to lie down (to sleep)”; ītamar ← amāru I “to see”; šanītam ← šanītu I “a second time jB”
  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 OB "II" 6; L I.4 OB "SM" a+23'; L I.4 MB "Priv₁" 6; L I.4 MB "Priv₁" 31; cf. L I.4 SB "I" 271
BabaOB1 i 24. [i]t-ti-lam-ma i-ta-mar ša-ni-tam

25

  • N: [i]tbe | ītawwâm | ana ummīšu
  • T: He arose to talk to his mother:
  • L: [i]tbe ← tebû I “OAkk, Ass. tabā'u(m), NB tabû to get up, arise, set out”; ītawwâm ← awû I “to speak”; ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; ummīšu ← ummu I “f. mother”
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "SM" a+4'; L I.4 MB "Priv₁" 7; cf. L I.4 SB "I" 243; cf. L I.4 SB "I" 272
BabaOB1 i 25. [i]t-be₂ i-ta-wa-a-am a-na um-mi-šu

26

  • N: ummī | ātamar | šanītam
  • T: ‘O mother, I have seen another.
  • L: ummī ← ummu I “f. mother”; ātamar ← amāru I “to see”; šanītam ← šanītu I “a second time jB”
  • Parallels: L I.4 SB "I" 274
BabaOB1 i 26. [um]-mi# a#-ta#-mar ša-ni-tam

27-28

  • N: [ ... ] ... | ina sūqim | [ša uru]k | ribītim
  • T: [...] … in the street of Uruk-the-City,
  • L: ina ← ina I “(im-m..., ip-p... etc.) in, on”; sūqim ← sūqu I “pl. m. & f. street Bab., NA”; [ša ← ša I “who(m), which”; uru]k ← Uruk I; ribītim ← rebītu I
  • Parallels: L I.4 OB "III" 174; L I.4 SB "I" 275; L I.4 MB "Priv₁" 33
BabaOB1 i 27-28. [x x x] me?-e UL.A i-na su₂-qi₂-im | [ša uru]k{ki} ri-bi-tim

29-30

  • N: haṣṣinnu(m) | nadī-ma || elīšu | pahrū
  • T: an axe was lying and (people) were gathered around it.
  • L: haṣṣinnu(m) ← haṣṣinnu I “Mari, NB pl. f. axe of copper, silver, gold etc.”; nadī-ma ← nadû III “to throw (down)”; elīšu ← eli I “on, over, above”; pahrū ← pahāru II “to gather”
  • Parallels: L I.4 SB "I" 276; L I.4 MB "Priv₁" 34
BabaOB1 i 29-30. ha#-aṣ#-ṣi#-nu na-di-i-ma | e-li-šu pa-ah-ru

31

  • N: haṣṣinnum-ma | šani | būnūšu
  • T: The axe itself, its appearance was strange;
  • L: haṣṣinnum-ma ← haṣṣinnu I “Mari, NB pl. f. axe of copper, silver, gold etc.”; šani ← šanû IV “to be changed, become different”; būnūšu ← būnu II “goodness”
BabaOB1 i 31. ha-aṣ-ṣi-nu-um-ma ša-ni bu-nu-šu

32

  • N: āmuršū-ma | ahtadu | anāku
  • T: I saw it and became glad.
  • L: āmuršū-ma ← amāru I “to see”; ahtadu ← hadû III “to be joyful, rejoice”; anāku ← anāku I “I”
BabaOB1 i 32. a-mur-šu-ma ah-ta-du a-na-ku

33-34

  • N: arāmšū-ma | kīma aššatim || ahabbub | elšu
  • T: I loved it like a wife, caressing and embracing it,
  • L: arāmšū-ma ← râmu II “to love”; kīma ← kīma I “like”; aššatim ← aššatu I “wife”; ahabbub ← habābu I “to murmur, chirp, twitter Bab.”; elšu ← eli I “on, over, above”
  • Parallels: L I.4 SB "I" 282; L I.4 MB "Priv₁" 37; L I.4 SB "II" 254; cf. L I.4 SB "II" 265; cf. L I.4 SB "II" 269; cf. L I.4 SB "II" 287
BabaOB1 i 33-34. a-ra-am-šu-ma ki-ma aš-ša-tim | a-ha-ab-bu-ub el-šu

35-36

  • N: elqēšū-ma | aštakanšu | ana ahīya
  • T: I took it up and put it at my side.’
  • L: elqēšū-ma ← leqû II “to take, take over”; aštakanšu ← šakānu I “to put, place, lay down”; ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; ahīya ← ahu II “arm, side (st. constr. ah(i))”
BabaOB1 i 35-36. el-qe₂-šu-ma aš-ta-ka-an-šu | a-na a-hi-ia

37-38

  • N: ummi (|) gilgāmeš | emqet | mūdât | kalāma | īde | [issaqqaram] | a[na gilgāmeš]
  • T: The mother of Gilgameš, well versed in everything, [said] to [Gilgameš]
  • L: ummi ← ummu I “f. mother”; gilgāmeš ← Gilgameš I; emqet ← emqu I “f. emuqtu wise, clever Bab.”; mūdât ← mūdû I “pl. mūdû, NB mūdānê”; kalāma ← kalāma I “all (of it) Bab. indeclinable as obj. of vb. or gen. after st. constr.”; īde ← edû II “to know (M/NA cf. wadûm)”; [issaqqaram] ← zakāru I “to speak, say”; a[na ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; gilgāmeš] ← Gilgameš I
  • Parallels: L I.4 SB "I" 284; cf. L I.4 MB "Priv₁" 38

  • N: ūmī (|) sebet || u sebe (|) mušiātim
  • T: For seven days and seven nights
  • L: ūmī ← ūmu I “pl. m. & f. day”; sebet ← sebe I “f. sebet(tu) seven, sebet ūmim sebe mušiātim seven days (and)…”; u ← u I “and, but, also”; sebe ← sebe I “f. sebet(tu) seven, sebet ūmim sebe mušiātim seven days (and)…”; mušiātim ← mušītu I “pl. mušiātu, mušâtu night(-time)”
  • Note: See [RN117: 183]: “It is conventional to restore ‘six days and seven nights’ in this line, following the example of SB I “194” [192]. However, the evidence now suggests that where the late text has this formulation the OB text had ‘seven days and seven nights’ (undamaged in OB VA + BM ii 8'; see Ch. 13, the commentary on SB XI 128), and so the broken numeral is here read 7 instead of 6. A stray wedge after this numeral, not seen by previous copyists, is not convincingly the remains of a KAM (cf. I. 56), and is ignored as an error” [courtesy Ll. Feliu].
  • Parallels: L I.4 SB "I" 192
